fixes.explanation: That's the word, baker. "Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth…" (Genesis 6:5). The verse keeps going and says every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time. I think this is one of the hard spots in the passage. The LORD sees all of it, and I'd rather read it slowly than rush past it.

That's right, baker. The LORD says, "I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth…" (Genesis 6:7). Then He adds that He is grieved that He made them. I think that's the part to sit with. This isn't a LORD who shrugs. The text says He was grieved in His heart (Genesis 6:6), and that makes this verse hit harder.
